content.text: The deterministic period check will keep firing on the spelled-out "ninety days"; per the verifier that is a phrasing artifact, not a substantive shortfall, and it does not warrant a redline. The one substantive item to repair is the overstatement about the hosted-Services warranty.

input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
input.rationale: Compliant at the preferred position; no redline and no counterparty comment proposed. (1) Duration: 19.2 warrants Deliverable conformity for ninety days - i.e. 90 days, three months - measured from the later of delivery or acceptance, and hosted Services must conform throughout the subscription term. The 90-day Deliverable period meets the preferred services/deliverable standard, and the term-long hosted-Services warranty satisfies the preferred software-conformance requirement (it runs for as long as Customer subscribes rather than a fixed 12-month window). The automated period check failed only because the document spells the number out as "ninety days" instead of "90" or "ninety (90)"; that is a drafting-style artifact, not a shortfall below the 90-day threshold, so it is noted here as internal evidence rather than raised as a negotiation issue. (2) Standard of performance: 19.1 warrants Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel in accordance with industry standards, the Agreement and each Order Form, plus material conformity of Services and Deliverables to documentation and agreed specifications. (3) Remedy: 19.4 tracks the model remedy - prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, and if Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period, termination of the affected item and refund of Fees paid for it - and is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. (4) Additional warranties: 19.3 covers malicious code intentionally introduced by Vendor, compliance with Applicable Law, no material diminution of functionality, and no contaminating open-source use. (5) Disclaimer: no "AS IS" language appears anywhere in the Agreement; 19.5 is confined to implied warranties and expressly provides that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality duty, data-protection duty or stated remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties and walk-away territory is not implicated. Section 6.2 supplies a further refund right after two failed correction cycles.
